channel.title: InvestPR Media Monitoring
channel.description: The standout news was Envocore's $129 million, five-year PRASA contract to modernize water metering across all 78 municipalities, alongside a newly surfaced $1.1 billion Army Corps award to Ferrovial for Río Piedras channel work — Puerto Rico's largest-ever civil works contract. Retail investment continued with Five Below confirming a 2027 Puerto Rico entry and TJ Maxx and Zimmermann opening new stores, while FY2026 General Fund revenue rose $279 million on stronger corporate tax collections. Real risks persist: an island-wide water/drought emergency continues with well-reactivation funding still pending Fiscal Oversight Board approval, and tariff costs paid by Puerto Rico jumped 289% to $919.7 million in 2025. The Fiscal Oversight Board's own composition also remains contested amid PREPA bankruptcy politics, an unresolved governance risk for investors watching the energy sector.
